summary: Production request fan-out cascade causing API 5xx/429 surge and customer payment flow degradation
description: Issue summary: At 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC we observed a rapid increase in 5xx errors and 429s for customer ArborBank leading to slowed payment verification flows. Traffic analysis showed per-request amplification (fan-out) from the API gateway to multiple backend serving shards, which created token emission backlogs and triggered per-customer rate-limiting. Impact: ArborBank experienced ~40% request slowdowns for payment path calls over a ~35 minute window; non-payment traffic (other customers) saw elevated tail latencies but significantly fewer errors due to per-customer circuit breakers. Timeline and key events are in the timeline field below. This ticket captures the immediate mitigation and longer-term follow-ups.
timeline: 2026-03-10 02:05 UTC - ArborBank CS reported increased latency for payment verification via #support-arborbank in Slack.
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Automated alerts: api-gateway 5xx rate increased, multiplexer queue depth > 1200.
2026-03-10 02:18 UTC - Incident declared (Sev0). Initial triage started by on-call.
2026-03-10 02:23 UTC - Temporary per-customer fanout cap of 4 requests applied in gateway (hotfix), immediate reduction in new amplification observed.
2026-03-10 02:28 UTC - Autoscaler attempted to add serving nodes but collided with a tagging mismatch; manual scale-up performed.
2026-03-10 02:40 UTC - Rate limit tripping reduced to baseline; ArborBank payment flows returned to normal by 02:50 UTC.
2026-03-10 03:15 UTC - Root cause identified; rollback of recent multiplexer routing-splat change completed.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Post-incident follow-up meeting; action items assigned and scheduled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a single request to the /v1/generate endpoint with header X-Routing-Mode: fanout and an upstream client that sets batch=all. 2) Observe that the gateway expands the request into N downstream multiply-targeted calls when routing-splat config is enabled. 3) Under high concurrency this causes multiplexer queue depth to grow and backend 5xxs as token emission backlog increases.
investigation_notes: Gateway logs show header 'X-Routing-Mode: fanout' being respected by a new routing-splat rule introduced in routing PR #782 which incorrectly treated missing shard filters as wildcard targets.
Serving runtime reported increased KV cache evictions while queue depth > 900 which amplified per-token latency.
Autoscaler failed to label new instances due to a tag name mismatch introduced in an unrelated infra change (INT-5021).
Billing observed spike in per-token charge for ArborBank during the incident window; finance notified to suppress anomalous charges pending review.
root_cause: A recently deployed routing-splat configuration (PR #782) allowed wildcard expansion when a per-request shard filter was omitted. Combined with an ArborBank client header pattern that set batch=all, the gateway expanded individual requests into multiple downstream calls (fan-out). The multiplexer and serving runtime were not configured with a per-customer fanout cap, which permitted amplification until per-customer rate-limits and autoscaler interventions kicked in. An unrelated autoscaler tagging regression (INT-5021) slowed scale-up, worsening the backlog and causing backend 5xxs.
mitigation: 1) Hotfix: applied gateway guardrail to cap per-request fanout to 4 targets at 2026-03-10 02:23 UTC. 2) Rolled back the routing-splat change to the previous stable config at 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC. 3) Manually scaled serving cluster for ArborBank to add capacity while autoscaler tag bug was fixed. 4) Suspended anomalous billing for ArborBank during incident window.
resolution: Hotfix and rollback restored normal behavior; ArborBank confirmed payment flows recovered. Incident closed after verification of traffic stabilization for 30 minutes and no recurrence in following 24 hours. Customer follow-up call held on 2026-03-11. Root cause and remediation plan communicated to ArborBank CSM.
postincident_action_items: Apply persistent gateway validation to reject ambiguous routing headers (owner: gateway team, due: 2026-03-20)
Add per-customer fanout cap as a configurable policy (owner: routing team, due: 2026-03-24)
Fix autoscaler tagging regression and add CI check to prevent future tag name mismatches (owner: infra team, due: 2026-03-18)
Create synthetic test that exercises batch=all + routing-splat combinations in staging (owner: qa, due: 2026-03-16)
Finance to issue credit for anomalous token charges and confirm completion (owner: finance, due: 2026-03-15)
Update runbook with fanout detection and mitigation steps (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-14)
